QF.id: IV Fixed Income Instruments and Bond Markets_2

question.text: A 10-year, 9% annual coupon bond has a face value of Rs. 100. If the required yield is 10%, what is the approximate bond price?

explanation.text: The Logic: Price = PV of annual coupons + PV of face value = 9 x [1 - (1.10)^-10] / 0.10 + 100 / (1.10)^10 = 9 x 6.1446 + 100 x 0.3855 = 55.30 + 38.55 = Rs. 93.86 (approx). Because the required yield (10%) exceeds the coupon rate (9%), the bond trades at a discount to par. The Trap: Rs. 100.00 would be the price only if the required yield equalled the coupon rate (a par bond). Rs. 106.42 is close to the value when the required yield is below the coupon rate, i.e. a premium bond. Rs. 88.70 over-discounts the cash flows.
